result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Choosing, Checking and Reporting" subtitle: "Design checklist · common errors · lonely PSUs · sample size · reporting survey results · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 1 to 4: design, descriptive estimates, regression, weights - Today: **put it together**: choose, check, plan and report ::: # Topic 1 — Choosing {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Three analyses of the same prevalence ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p0 <- mean(resp$hypertension) des_w <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~weight, data = resp) tibble(analysis = c("naive (no design)", "weights only", "full design"), estimate = c(p0, coef(svymean(~hypertension, des_w))[[1]], coef(svymean(~hypertension, des))[[1]]), se = c(sqrt(p0 * (1 - p0) / nrow(resp)), SE(svymean(~hypertension, des_w))[[1]], SE(svymean(~hypertension, des))[[1]])) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 4))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 analysis estimate se 1 naive (no design) 0.233 0.0098 2 weights only 0.200 0.0096 3 full design 0.200 0.0149 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **Weights** change the **estimate** (0.233 to 0.200). **Clusters** change the **SE** (0.0096 to 0.0149). Only the **full design** is correct for a population report. ::: ## Design effects differ by outcome ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sapply(c("hypertension", "diabetes", "smoker"), function(v) deff(svymean(as.formula(paste0("~", v)), des, deff = TRUE))[[1]]) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` hypertension diabetes smoker 2.60 1.11 1.57 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Hypertension 2.6**, smoking 1.6, diabetes 1.1 - The DEFF is large when the outcome **varies between PSUs** (the ICC from Clustered Data!) - No single design effect for the survey: report it **per outcome** ::: # Topic 2 — Checking {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Common errors ::: {.bad} - **Not declaring the design**, or declaring only weights - The **wrong weight** (household vs women's vs men's module) - **`filter()`** then re-declaring, instead of `subset()` - **`chisq.test()`, `lm()`, `median()`** on survey data - Reporting **weighted n** as the sample size - Ignoring **missing data** in the weights or the analysis variables ::: ## Lonely PSUs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} resp |> filter(diabetes == 1, age < 45) |> distinct(stratum, psu) |> count(stratum) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 8 × 2 stratum n 1 East Rural 1 2 East Urban 3 3 North Rural 2 4 North Urban 3 5 South Rural 4 6 South Urban 5 7 West Rural 2 8 West Urban 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} In small subgroups some strata contain **only one PSU**: a variance cannot be computed from one cluster (a "**lonely PSU**"). Keep the **full design** with `subset()`. If it still happens, `options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")` (or `"average"`, `"certainty"`) gives a conservative variance. Better: **merge strata** or use a larger group. ::: # Topic 3 — Planning and reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Sample size for a survey ::: {.eq} n (survey) = n (simple random sample) × DEFF ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(srs = 1000, survey = 1000 * 2.2, effective_now = round(nrow(resp) / deff(svymean(~hypertension, des, deff = TRUE))[[1]])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` srs survey effective_now 1000 2200 714 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - A precision that needs **1,000** under simple random sampling needs about **2,200** with a design effect of 2.2 - Our 1,853 respondents are worth about **710** independent adults - More **PSUs** help more than more adults per PSU - Plan for **nonresponse** too: invite 1,000 / 0.74 to get 1,000 respondents ::: ## Reporting survey results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} resp |> as_survey_design(ids = psu, strata = stratum, weights = weight, nest = TRUE) |> group_by(region) |> summarise(n = unweighted(n()), prevalence = survey_mean(hypertension, vartype = "ci")) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 5 region n prevalence prevalence_low prevalence_upp 1 East 439 0.189 0.119 0.259 2 North 452 0.19 0.149 0.232 3 South 480 0.232 0.158 0.306 4 West 482 0.186 0.138 0.235 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.good} - **Describe the design**: strata, PSUs, stages, weights, nonresponse adjustment - **Unweighted n** and **weighted** estimates with **95% CI** - **Design effect** (or effective n) for key outcomes - **Response rate** - Software and options (`survey` package, lonely PSU option) ::: ## An example sentence ::: {.key} *Example:* "Hypertension prevalence was 20.0% (95% CI 17.1 to 23.1; design effect 2.6; 1,853 respondents in 48 PSUs; response rate 74%), estimated with survey-weighted analysis in R (survey package)." ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `survey-workshop/labs/lab5_report.R` - three analyses side by side, design effects - sample size with the design effect - lonely PSUs, reporting table and one-sentence result ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="v5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="pu88ce.jr72tz" data-show="VGhlIG9uZSB0aGF0IGRlY2xhcmVzIHdlaWdodHMsIHN0cmF0YSBhbmQgUFNVcyB3aXRoIHN2 eWRlc2lnbg==" data-explain="V2VpZ2h0cyBhcmUgbmVlZGVkIGZvciB0aGUgZXN0aW1hdGUgYW5kIHRoZSBmdWxsIGRlc2ln biBmb3IgdGhlIHZhcmlhbmNlLiBXZWlnaHRzIHdpdGhvdXQgY2x1c3RlcnMgZ2l2ZSBhIHBy ZWNpc2UtbG9va2luZyBidXQgbWlzbGVhZGluZyBpbnRlcnZhbC4="} Which analysis of the prevalence is appropriate for a report on the whole population? - The unweighted mean with a simple random sample standard error - The one that declares weights, strata and PSUs with svydesign - A weighted mean with a standard error that ignores the PSUs - The mean of the PSU means with a standard error of 1.96 ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="v5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="pu8ll4.jr7hbd" data-show="QWJvdXQgMiwyMDAgcmVzcG9uZGVudHM=" data-explain="VGhlIHNhbXBsZSBzaXplIGlzIG11bHRpcGxpZWQgYnkgdGhlIGRlc2lnbiBlZmZlY3Q6IDEs MDAwIHggMi4yID0gMiwyMDAgcmVzcG9uZGVudHMsIGJlZm9yZSBhbGxvd2luZyBmb3Igbm9u cmVzcG9uc2Uu"} A precision needs 1,000 respondents under simple random sampling. About how many does a survey with DEFF 2.2 need? - About 1,000 respondents - About 455 respondents - About 2,200 respondents - About 3,200 respondents ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="v5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="pu8ytu.jr7vsr" data-show="QSBzdHJhdHVtIHdpdGggb25lIFBTVSBnaXZlcyBubyB2YXJpYW5jZSwgc28ga2VlcCB0aGUg ZnVsbCBkZXNpZ24gd2l0aCBzdWJzZXQoKQ==" data-explain="QSB2YXJpYW5jZSB3aXRoaW4gYSBzdHJhdHVtIG5lZWRzIGF0IGxlYXN0IHR3byBQU1VzLiBT dWJzZXR0aW5nIHRoZSBkZXNpZ24sIHJhdGhlciB0aGFuIHRoZSBkYXRhLCBrZWVwcyBhbGwg dGhlIFBTVXM7IHRoZSBsb25lbHkucHN1IG9wdGlvbiBoYW5kbGVzIHRoZSByZXN0Lg=="} What is a lonely PSU and what should you do? - A PSU that contains a single respondent, which should then be dropped from the sample - A PSU that is in no stratum, which should be assigned to the nearest stratum - A stratum without any respondents, which should be removed from the design - A stratum with one PSU gives no variance, so keep the full design with subset() ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="v5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="pu9c2g.jr8aa1" data-show="VGhlIHdlaWdodGVkIGVzdGltYXRlIHdpdGggaXRzIENJLCB0aGUgdW53ZWlnaHRlZCBuIGFu ZCB0aGUgREVGRg==" data-explain="UmVhZGVycyBuZWVkIHRvIGtub3cgdGhlIHByZWNpc2lvbiBhbmQgaG93IG1hbnkgcmVzcG9u ZGVudHMgdGhlIGVzdGltYXRlIHJlc3RzIG9uLiBUaGUgd2VpZ2h0ZWQgbiBpcyB0aGUgcG9w dWxhdGlvbiBzaXplLCBub3QgdGhlIHNhbXBsZSBzaXplLg=="} Which set of information is best to report with a survey estimate? - The weighted estimate with its CI, the unweighted n and the DEFF - The weighted estimate, with the sum of the weights as the sample size - The unweighted estimate, with a CI from a simple random sample of adults - The weighted estimate alone, since weights already include the design ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="v5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="pu9pb6.jr8orf" data-show="SXQgZGVwZW5kcyBvbiBob3cgbXVjaCBlYWNoIG91dGNvbWUgdmFyaWVzIGJldHdlZW4gUFNV cw==" data-explain="Q2x1c3RlcmluZyBtYXR0ZXJzIHdoZW4gdGhlIG91dGNvbWUgaXMgbW9yZSBhbGlrZSB3aXRo aW4gYSBQU1UgdGhhbiBiZXR3ZWVuIFBTVXMsIHdoaWNoIGlzIGEgcHJvcGVydHkgb2YgdGhl IG91dGNvbWUgKGl0cyBJQ0MpLCBzbyB0aGUgZGVzaWduIGVmZmVjdCB2YXJpZXMgYnkgb3V0 Y29tZS4="} Why does the design effect differ between hypertension (2.6) and diabetes (1.1)? - Diabetes has less missing data than hypertension in the survey - It depends on how much each outcome varies between PSUs - Hypertension was measured on a larger sample of adults - The design effect is larger for continuous variables than binary ones ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - Weights fix the **estimate**; clusters fix the **SE** - Report the **design**, **unweighted n**, **CI**, **DEFF** and **response rate** - **Lonely PSUs**: `subset()`, merge strata, `survey.lonely.psu` - **Sample size** = n (SRS) × DEFF, and allow for nonresponse - Different outcomes, different **design effects** ::: **Next:** Cheat sheet and the next module

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
